observations.title: Accounting errors overstated the Cash-in-Bank (CiB) accounts by P51.371 million mainly because of the: (a) absence of an effective reconciliation of the records of the Office of the City Accountant (OCAT) and City Treasurer’s Office (CTO); (b) inability of the accounting application to capture the standard transaction descriptions and references and produce the prescribed primary and subsidiary records that provide the audit trails; and (c) breakdowns in the bank reconciliation. Thus, overstated the carrying amounts of the CiB accounts by a net amount of P51.371 million.
observations.description:
1.1 The City maintained 79 bank accounts in CY 2021, as shown in Table 1.

Table 1 - Number of bank accounts maintained by the City in CY 2021

| Account | General Fund (GF) | Special Education Fund (SEF) | Trust Fund (TF) | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CiB-Local Currency Current Account (CiB-LCCA) | 5 | 1 | 10 | 16 |
| CiB-LCCA Expropriation Accounts | 48 | - | - | 48 |
| CiB-Local Currency Time Deposit (CiB-LCTD) | 6 | 3 | 5 | 14 |
| CiB-Foreign Currency Savings Account (CiB-FCSA) | - | - | 1 | 1 |
| Total | 59 | 4 | 16 | 79 |

1.2 The Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2021, reported the carrying amount of the CiB at P10,833,846,963 (Table 2) which represents 17.32 percent of the Total Assets as of the same date of P62,542,872,024.44.

Table 2 - Carrying amounts of CiB accounts as of December 31, 2021

| Account | GF | SEF | TF | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CiB-LCCA | P2,989,023,591.82 | P2,251,690,537.86 | P2,561,332,713.20 | P7,802,046,842.88 |
| CiB-LCTD | 1,437,141,010.12 | 974,523,017.75 | 619,878,180.44 | 3,031,542,208.31 |
| CiB-FCSA | - | - | 257,912.20 | 257,912.20 |
| Total | P4,426,164,601.94 | P3,226,213,555.61 | P3,181,468,805.84 | P10,833,846,963.39 |

1.3 We tested the validity, existence, accuracy and completeness of these CiB accounts to determine if they have been accounted for in accordance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS). Our tests included, among others, evaluation of controls, vouching and verification of underlying transactions, confirmation of balances and account analysis. The audit results showed that accounting errors overstated the carrying amounts of the CiB accounts by a net amount of P51.371 million (Table 3).

Table 3 - Accounting errors that overstated the CiB accounts

| Error Description | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Checks issued not recognized in the books of accounts | (P31,217,321.18) |
| Net overstatement on account of unrecognized deposits, withdrawals and other errors - GF | (12,534,572.43) |
| Net overstatement on account of unrecognized debit memos - SEF | (645,894.46) |
| Net overstatement on account of unrecognized deposits, withdrawals, credit memos and debit memos - TF | (6,973,693.45) |
| Net overstatement of the CiB accounts | (P51,371,481.52) |
| Percentage of total assets of P62,542,872,024.44 | .08 |

Checks issued not recognized in the books - P31.217 million

1.4 Section 43 of Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), Volume I, provides:

Reporting of Checks Issued. – The checks released to claimants shall be reported in the Report of Checks Issued (RCI) which shall be prepared daily by the Treasurer for each fund. It shall be submitted to the Accountant for preparation of Journal of Entry Voucher based on individual checks issued and recording in the Check Disbursements Journal.

1.5 We tested the accuracy and completeness of the carrying amounts of the CiB accounts by: (a) matching the checks issued per RCI with those taken up the Check Disbursement Journal (CkDJ) and paid checks returned by the banks (underlying the bank statements); and (b) performing comparative analysis of the CiB balances per bank, books of accounts of the CGM and CTO; and (c) tracing and comparing the checks issued per CkDJ to the general ledgers (GLs)/subsidiary ledgers (SLs).

1.6 The result showed checks issued which were not recognized in the accounts amounting to P31,217,321.18 (Table 4).

Table 4 - Checks issued in not recognized in the CiB accounts

| Particulars | No. of Checks | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Checks NOT in the CkDJ: |  |  |
| GF | 729 | P25,747,624.25 |
| SEF | 30 | 169,005.51 |
| TF | 65 | 5,300,691.42 |
| Checks issued not recognized in the books of accounts | 824 | P31,217,321.18 |

1.7 This came about mainly because of the: (a) absence of an effective reconciliation of the records of the OCAT and CTO; (b) inability of the accounting application used by the OCAT (PPSAS System) to capture the standard transaction description and references and produce the prescribed primary and subsidiary records that provide the audit trail; and (c) breakdown of the bank reconciliation as reconciling items are either not acted upon timely or not acted upon at all. These causes are evident in the accounting deficiencies discussed in the succeeding sub-paragraphs.

a. Checks issued by batch were not sequentially recorded in the CkDJ since the PPSAS System only captures the first check number of the batch. However, corrective measures (e.g., indicating the series of the checks in the Payee and Particulars columns of the CkDJ) were not done by the OCAT.

b. Certain transactions were erroneously posted/encoded in the CkDJ (Table 5):

Table 5 - Errors Noted in Posting/Encoding in the CkDJ

| Fund | GF |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Quantity | Amount |
| No amount | 22 | - |
| Erroneously recorded in CkDJ | 10 | - |
| Not in CTO RCI but recorded in OCAT RCI | 2 | P50,980.00 |
| Total | 34 | P50,980.00 |

c. There were checks recorded in the CkDJ but not found in the appertaining RCI (Table 6). Available information/documents did not permit the Audit Team to establish, among others, if these are mere errors in encoding or if these were in fact checks issued not captured in the RCI.

Table 6 - Checks recorded in the CkDJ but not found in the appertaining RCI

| Fund | Quantity | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GF | 11 | P28,480.00 |
| TF | 1 | 2,000.00 |
| Total | 12 | P30,480.00 |

1.8 Moreover, the CTO and OCAT submitted separate Reports of Checks Issued (RCI) totaling P24,421,756,558.56 and P24,014,487,669.07, respectively, thus, a discrepancy of P407,268,889.49. For instance, in accounting for the discrepancy, Check Nos. 7483557 and 1128500 under GF amounting to P22,500.00 and P28,480.00, respectively, were found in the OCAT RCI but not in the CTO’s.

1.9 The checks issued not recognized in the accounts are perceptible in the comparative analysis of the RCI and GLs/ SLs as the latter (books of final entries) are lesser by a net amount of P161,243,715.42 (Table 7).

Table 7 - Comparative analysis of the RCI and GL/SL

| Fund | CiB-LCCA GL/SL (a) | CkDJ (b) | RCI (c) | RCI v. GL/SL (c-a) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GF | P17,939,940,341.58 | P17,939,940,341.58 | P18,083,149,527.38 | P143,209,185.80 |
| SEF | 2,213,106,032.11 | 2,213,106,032.11 | 2,223,078,943.59 | 9,972,911.48 |
| TF | 4,107,466,469.45 | 4,107,466,469.45 | 4,115,528,087.59 | 8,061,618.14 |
| Total | P24,260,512,843.14 | P24,260,512,843.14 | P24,421,756,558.56 | P161,243,715.42 |

1.10 The absence of an effective reconciliation of the records of the OCAT and CTO as well as the breakdown in the bank reconciliation is evident in the material differences among the balances per bank, per CTO records and per books (Table 8):

Table 8 - Comparative balances per bank, books of accounts and Records of the CTO

| Fund/Account | Books vs. Bank | Books vs. Treasury | Bank vs. Treasury |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GF CiB- LCCA | (P386,974,734.91) | P 35,159,868.98 | P422,134,603.89 |
| GF CiB- LCTD | (1,275,369.53) | (2,870,527.34) | (1,595,157.81) |
| SEF CiB- LCCA | 622,238.96 | 2,465,253.23 | 1,843,014.27 |
| SEF CiB- LCTD | 21,548.04 | - | (21,548.04) |
| TF CiB- LCCA | 6,373,651.45 | 395,032,157.97 | 388,658,506.52 |
| TF CiB- LCTD | - | (712,164.10) | (712,164.10) |
| Total All Funds | (P381,232,665.99) | P429,074,588.74 | P810,307,254.73 |

1.11 The breakdown in bank reconciliation is further evident in the submission of the CY 2021 BRS which was delayed by 4 to 616 days.

1.12 The inability of OCAT to provide certain documents supporting the movements in CiB accounts and the deficiencies in the PPSAS System hindered the Audit Team to fully account for the differences in the accounting and treasury records.

Net overstatement on account of (i) unrecognized deposits, withdrawals, credit memos and debit memos; and (ii) other errors - P20.154 million

1.13 Review and verification of the Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) showed that, contrary to the procedures prescribed under COA Circular No. 96-011, journal vouchers to record all valid reconciling items therein requiring adjustments and corrections are not promptly prepared by the OCAT.

1.14 The book reconciling items listed in the City’s BRS amounted to P12,534,572.43, P645,894.46 and P6,973,693.45 under the GF, SEF and TF, respectively, or a total of P20,154,160.34. These book reconciling items pertain to the transactions in CYs 2014 to 2021 and are errors in accounting for the CiB which the OCAT itself identified. To date, however, these errors have remained uncorrected.

1.15 We emphasized that the preparation of BRS is not in finding the amounts of discrepancies in order to reconcile both records, but in investigating the validity of each reconciling item and promptly recording the necessary adjustments in the books of accounts.

1.16 We have already pointed out the foregoing accounting errors in CYs 2019 and 2020 Annual Audit Reports of the City as well and identified in these reports the causes.

recommendations.label: a.
recommendations.text: Direct the OCAT to correct the accounting errors which resulted in overstatement of the carrying amounts of the CiB accounts by a net amount of P51.371 million;
recommendations.lead_in: We reiterated our recommendation that Management:

recommendations.label: b.
recommendations.text: Direct the OCAT and CTO to reconcile fully their CiB records with those of the depository banks; and
recommendations.lead_in: We reiterated our recommendation that Management:

recommendations.label: c.
recommendations.text: Address the deficiencies of the PPSAS System used by OCAT to ensure that it captures, processes and reports all disbursement transactions of the City with the standard audit trails.
recommendations.lead_in: We reiterated our recommendation that Management:

recommendations.text: We also recommended that Management fast track the implementation of the new accounting application system for efficient, valid, accurate and complete processing of financial transactions.

observations.title: The City had not settled cash advances totaling P182.725 million contrary to Section 89 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997, and bear on the fair presentation of the affected accounts in the FS.
observations.description:
2.1 We audited the cash advances of the City pursuant to Section 89 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997, to establish the regularity and propriety of the grant and liquidation of cash advances and the fair presentation in the FS of the affected accounts. Our procedures included, among others, verification of postings, evaluation and verification of grant and liquidation of cash advances made during the year.

2.2 The cash advance account balances as of December 31, 2021 show the total unliquidated amounts of P182,724,953.85, out of which P95,424,136.86 represents cash advances of employees who had retired, resigned, deceased and gone AWOL and, mostly, have been outstanding for more than three years.

2.3 The non-liquidation of these advances is not in keeping with the prescribed period of liquidation. An Accountable Officer is required to liquidate his cash advance as soon as the purpose for which it was given has been served. Except for petty cash fund, all cash advances shall be fully liquidated at the end of each year.

2.4 These unliquidated advances (Table 9) were intended to defray the expenses/disbursements for the year in which they were granted, thus, the expenses/disbursements paid out of them had not been recognized in the books of accounts in the year incurred. This weigh on the fair presentation of the affected accounts in the FS.

| Table 9 - Accounts affected by the non-liquidation of cash advances |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prior Years | Current Year | Total | Account |
| - | P12,778,484.00 | P 12,778,484.00 | Donations |
| - | 6,309,707.92 | 6,309,707.92 | Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses |
| P163,636,761.93 | - | 163,636,761.93 | Government Equity |
| P163,636,761.93 | P19,088,191.92 | P182,724,953.85 |  |

Liquidations not yet recorded by OCAT

2.5 Replies to the Demand Letters dated April 11 and 13, 2022, which were sent to the concerned accountable officials (AO) and employees informed that the liquidations of the cash advances in the amount of P641,630.33 have already been submitted to the OCAT. Thus, the OCAT has not yet recorded these liquidations in the books of accounts.

recommendations.label: a.
recommendations.text: Enforce the liquidation of the cash advances and, henceforth, enforce strictly the liquidation of cash advances within the prescribed period; and

recommendations.label: b.
recommendations.text: Record in the book of accounts the liquidations of cash advances amounting P641,630.33 and, prospectively, promptly record the liquidations of cash advances in order to reflect them in the books of accounts in the proper period.

observations.title: Payables amounting to P21.888 million were not supported with the required documents proving their validity, thus, casting doubt on the fairness of the presentation of the payable accounts in the City’s FS.
observations.description:
3.1 We audited the City’s Accounts Payable to ascertain if their carrying amounts presented in the FS as of December 31, 2021: (a) exist and are indeed firm liabilities of the City; (b) complete and accurately valued; (c) properly classified; and (d) have been accounted for in accordance with pertinent laws, rules and regulations and the IPSAS.

3.2 Our procedures include, among others, (i) vouching against procurement and disbursement documents; (ii) examination of procurement documents; (iii) cut-off test and other test of details, balances and disclosures; (iv) confirmation; and (v) account analysis.

3.3 As of December 31, 2021, Accounts Payable totaled P6,051,729,793.35 consisting of liabilities recognized during the year and in the prior year’s amounting to P3,429,599,139.32 and P2,622,130,654.03, respectively. (Tables 10 and 11)

Table 10 - Accounts Payable as of December 31, 2021

| Account | Accounts Payable recognized in 2021 | Accounts Payable recorded in Prior Years | Balance as of 12/31/2021 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts Payable | - | P 231,532.89 | P 231,532.89 |
| Accounts Payable - 2017 - Capital Outlay | - | 23,559,702.79 | 23,559,702.79 |
| Accounts Payable - 2018 - Capital Outlay | - | 116,207,283.86 | 116,207,283.86 |
| Accounts Payable 2019 - MOOE | - | 518,109,550.21 | 518,109,550.21 |
| Accounts Payable - 2019 Capital Outlay | - | 967,431,560.89 | 967,431,560.89 |
| Accounts Payable - 2020 MOOE | - | 552,372,367.49 | 552,372,367.49 |
| Accounts Payable - 2020 Capital Outlay | - | 442,282,907.24 | 442,282,907.24 |
| Accounts Payable Unclaimed Checks - 2020 | - | 1,935,748.66 | 1,935,748.66 |
| Accounts Payable - 2021 MOOE | P2,555,727,002.86 | - | 2,555,727,002.86 |
| Accounts Payable - 2021 Capital Outlay | 672,663,859.22 | - | 672,663,859.22 |
| Accounts Payable - TF | 3,662,081.02 | - | 3,662,081.02 |
| Accounts Payable Unclaimed Checks - 2021 | 197,546,196.22 | - | 197,546,196.22 |
| Total | P3,429,599,139.32 | P2,622,130,654.03 | P6,051,729,793.35 |

Table 11 - Comparative CYs 2021 and 2020 Payables

| Account | 2021 | 2020 | Change 2021 vs. 2020 | Percent Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GF | P 4,791,534,949.39 | P5,523,721,077.45 | (P732,186,128.06) | (13) |
| SEF | 1,060,712,899.08 | 747,643,342.92 | 313,069,556.16 | 42 |
| TF | 199,481,944.88 | 9,304,461.60 | 190,177,483.28 | 2044 |
| Total | P6,051,729,793.35 | P6,280,688,881.97 | (P228,939,088.62) | (4) |

3.4 Out of the P3,429,599,139.32 payables recognized in CY 2021, the OCAT set-up P939,392,724.43 at year end.

3.5 We examined and analyzed the documents supporting P939,392,724.43 of these payables which the OCAT were able to submit to the Audit Team on March 31, 2022. The result showed that payables amounting to P21,887,936.93 lacked the required documentations. These payables represent 0.4 percent of the total carrying amount of the Accounts Payable account as at year-end.

a. All these payables were not supported with the DV certified:

i. By the authorized Supervisor/Head of Department/Office that the expenses are necessary, lawful and incurred under his direct supervision; and

ii. By the City Accountant that the supporting documents are complete and proper.

b. These payables were not also supported with the required documents to prove their validity as shown in Table 12.

Table 12 - Lacking supporting documents

| Document Not Supporting the Payable | Payable Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Journal Entry Vouchers | P11,838,426.75 |
| Acceptance and Inspection Report (AIR) | 52,887.31 |
| Delivery Receipt | 6,389,602.26 |

c. Out of 35 confirmation letters we sent to the creditors, 13 were returned bearing the remarks “address not found/ addressee moved out/ changed office address/ no receiver.”

3.6 Aging analysis identified payables in the amount of P1,625,539,630.64 which were set in CYs 2017 to 2019 and have remained outstanding for two years or more as of December 31, 2021. The City has not shown that these are still firm liabilities to pay. It must be pointed out that payables which have been outstanding for two years or more and against which no actual claims, administrative or judicial, has been filed or which is not covered by perfected contracts on record may be reverted to the unappropriated surplus of the GF.

recommendations.lead_in: In order to present fairly the Accounts Payable account in the FS, we recommended that Management direct the OCAT, in coordination with the City General Services Office, to:

observations.title: Seven hundred twenty-three (723) cases of double payment of emergency subsidy/financial assistance to beneficiaries in COVID-19 lockdown translated to a total payment of P8.424 million in excess of the amounts legally authorized.
observations.description:
4.1 We audited the emergency subsidy/financial assistance for households COVID-19 lockdown funded by the National Government and transferred to the City of Manila in CYs 2020 to 2021 to determine if the distribution was in accordance with the laws, rules and regulations in Table 13.

Table 13 - COVID-19 Emergency Subsidy/Financial Assistance from the National Government

| Law, Rules and Regulations | Authorized Subsidy/Financial Assistance | Amount received from National Government | Amount distributed to the beneficiaries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RA No. 11464 or “Bayanihan to Recover As One Act” DSWD, DOLE, DTI, DA, DOF, DBM and DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 1, s. 2020 | Emergency subsidy of at least P5,000.00 to a maximum of P8,000.00 per month, per household, covering the months of April and May 2020 (Social Amelioration Program I (SAP I) | P1,485,440.000.00 | P1,473,725,000.00 (undistributed amount of P11,715,000.00 returned to DSWD-NCR on December 14, 2020 per Land Bank of the Philippines Check No. 1098352) |
| RA No. R.A. 11469 or “Bayanihan to Heal As One Act” DILG-DSWD-DND JMC No. 3, s. 2021 DBM LBC 136, s. 2021 DBM LBC 138, s. 2021 | Financial assistance of P1,000.00 per individual, with a maximum amount of P4,000.00 per family covering April and August 2021 | P3,046,556,000.00 | P3,046,556,000.00 |

4.2 The City informed that the Department of Social Work and Development (DSWD) provided the Manila Department of Social Welfare (MDSW) the list of the beneficiaries to be given the foregoing emergency subsidy/financial assistance.

4.3 These beneficiaries were divided into nine categories/groups, namely:

i. Baseco;

ii. District I;

iii. District II;

iv. District III;

v. District IV;

vi. District V;

vii. District VI;

viii. Transport Group (TG); and

ix. Informal Workers (IW).

Double payment of Emergency Subsidy - CY 2020

4.4 Using this list from the DSWD, the MDSW distributed the emergency subsidy for CY 2020 totaling P1,473,725,000.00 to 185,680 beneficiaries in COVID-19 lockdown.

a. Analysis and examination of the list of recipients showed 330 cases of double payment or 0.18 percent of emergency subsidy to 185,680 beneficiaries in COVID-19 lockdown. This resulted to a payment of P5.280 million or 0.36 percent of P1.474 billion over the amounts legally allowed (Table 14).

Double payment of Financial Assistance (FA) – CY 2021

4.5 The MDSW distributed the total FA of P3,046,556,000.00 to 380,820 beneficiaries in COVID-19 lockdown.

a. Audit of the list of recipients showed 393 cases of double payment or 0.10 percent of the FA to 380,820 beneficiaries. This translated to a total payment of P3.144 million or 0.10 percent of P3.047 billion in excess of the amounts legally authorized (Table 15).

4.6 For CYs 2020 to 2021, a total of 723 cases of double payment of emergency subsidy or FA resulted in the payment of P8.424 million in excess of the amounts legally prescribed.

4.7 The MDSW informed that, even prior to receiving the attendant Audit Observation Memorandum from the Audit Team, it had been looking into and investigating the unscrupulous beneficiaries who doubly claimed and received the emergency subsidy/financial assistance and that the verified cases of double payment have been forwarded to the City Legal Office (CLO). Inquiry showed that the CLO sent demand letters to these beneficiaries and three of them had already refunded, while two others issued promissory notes.

observations.title: The City has not implemented 11 Gender and Development (GAD) Programs/Projects/Activities (PPAs) with a total budget of P171.936 million, thus, foregoing the timely realization of the benefits expected therefrom.
observations.description:
5.1 Item C.8 of Philippine Commission on Women (PCW), Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG), Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and National Economic Development Authority (NEDA) Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-01 dated July 18, 2013 or the Guidelines on the Localization of the Magna Carta of Women (JMC No. 2013-01 for brevity), provides the guidelines on the preparation and submission of LGU GAD Accomplishment Reports (AR), such as:

(1) The GAD Focal Point System (GFPS) shall prepare their annual GAD AR based on the DILG-approved GAD Plan and Budget (GPB) or the enacted GPB following the form prescribed in Annex E. Activities completed until the end of the year may be included in the final LGU GAD AR.

5.2 The GPB and GAD AR of the City are being prepared by each department and submitted to the City Planning and Development Office for consolidation.

5.3 We are pleased to note that the CY 2021 GPB submitted to the Office of the Auditor on January 27, 2021, is compliant with the Magna Carta for Women that requires that the GAD budget shall be at least be five percent of the agency’s total budget appropriations. The City allocated for GAD P2,053,127,602.00 or 10.27 percent of the total CY 2021 appropriations of P20 billion. (Table 17).

| Total | P2,051,061,838.00 | P2,065,764.00 | - | 2,053,127,602.00 |

5.5 We are concerned that, as shown in Table 18:

a. the City was unable to implement 11 of the programmed GAD PPAs with a total budget of P171,936,252.00, thus, the City bypassed the timely realization of the benefits therefrom; and

b. the GFPS was unable to provide to the Audit Team the status of nine others considering that it has the duty and responsibility to regularly monitor the GAD budget to see if it is being spent for what it was intended for; and check on the actual cost of implementing the GAD activities.

5.6 The GFPS informed that the GAD trainings/seminars and other PPAs requiring onsite activities were unimplemented due to the COVID-19 pandemic wherein the City has implemented a work-from-home arrangement and reduced work force. We are of the view, however, that these PPAs could have been implemented to a certain extent based on PPAs of similar nature that the City implemented.

5.7 It is worthy to mention that, although the 11 planned PPAs were unimplemented, the City implemented 10 GAD PPAs other than those in the GPB with a budget of P309,565,545.00.

observations.title: The City has not remitted P38.408 million representing the amounts withheld as of December 31, 2021, for the accounts of the BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth, contrary to the appertaining legal prescriptions.
observations.section_heading: COMPLIANCE WITH TAX LAWS AND OTHER REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS / Due to Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Pag-IBIG and Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth)
observations.description:
6.1 Inter-Agency Payables are contributions due to/collections received/amounts withheld for remittance to the different government agencies. In the case of the City, these are payables to BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth.

6.2 Our audit of these accounts is guided by the following legal provisions:

Withholding and Remittance to BIR:

Executive Order No. 651 dated 16 February 1981 requires government offices, agencies and instrumentalities to comply strictly with the law and regulations in the withholding and remittance of internal revenue taxes imposed by the National Internal Revenue Code.

BIR Revenue Regulation (RR) No. 2-98, as amended, and RR No. 4-2002, as amended, require the remittance of withheld taxes within 10 days following the end of the month the withholding was made.

Withholding and Remittance to GSIS:

Section 6 of Republic Act (RA) No. 8291 or The GSIS Act of 1997 provides the guidelines in the collection and remittance of employee-members’ contributions.

Related thereto, COA issued Circular No. 2016-007 dated 7 March 2016 on the audit of GSIS premium deductions and remittances which was reiterated and extended to include audit of payments for GSIS monthly salary deductions and other loan amortization under COA Memorandum No. 2017-015 dated 8 August 2017.

Withholding and Remittance to Pag-IBIG:

Section 23 (a) of RA No. 9679 also known as An Act Further Strengthening the Home Development Mutual Fund, and for Other Purposes provides that it shall be the duty of every employer, private or public, to set aside and remit the contributions required under this Act in accordance with the mechanism determined by the Board of Trustees.

Withholding and Remittance to PhilHealth:

Section 11 of National Health Insurance Act of 2013 as amended by RA No. 9241 requires that the remittance of contribution shall be mandatory for all members. It shall be made to PhilHealth offices or to any of the accredited collecting agents. Failure to timely remit the appropriate premium contribution shall be subject to interest and penalties as prescribed by the Corporation without prejudice to other applicable penalties herein provided.

6.3 Analysis of the Inter-Agency Payables account as of December 31, 2021, showed that the City has not remitted P38,408,049.79 to the BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth contrary to the foregoing legal prescriptions. (Table 19)

Table 19 - Status of Remittances of Amounts Withheld for the Accounts of the BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Balance, January 1, 2021 | P224,218,741.89 | P107,687,322.74 | P39,045,637.18 | P23,966,182.19 |
| Add: Withheld in 2021 | 2,152,806,265.60 | 1,089,312,177.72 | 66,247,162.04 | 86,603,963.71 |
| Total | 2,377,025,007.49 | 1,196,999,500.46 | 105,292,799.22 | 110,570,145.90 |
| Less: Remittances in 2021 | 1,829,058,408.30 | 1,134,980,086.68 | 79,856,435.38 | 78,863,811.21 |
| Balance, December 31, 2021 | 547,966,599.19 | 62,019,413.78 | 25,436,363.84 | 31,706,334.69 |
| Remittances in 2022 | 534,266,958.23 | 49,690,311.60 | 16,431,739.11 | 28,331,652.77 |
| Unremitted Amount | P13,699,640.96 | P12,329,102.18 | P9,004,624.73 | P3,374,681.92 |
| TOTAL Unremitted Amount |  | P38,408,049.79 |  |  |

6.4 We noted that remittance of taxes and contributions withheld were not being made in full due to lack of thorough review of the documents and regular reconciliation of the remittances made against the deductions.

6.5 This may result to the imposition of interests, penalties and surcharges as well as difficulties on the part of the City personnel to avail of the services of the GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth.

recommendations.label: a.
recommendations.text: Direct the OCAT and CTO to remit the P38.408 million to the BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth without further delay; and

recommendations.label: b.
recommendations.text: Instruct them together with the City Personnel Office to, henceforth, ensure the correct and full remittance of the amounts withheld for the accounts of these agencies/corporations.
